title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. S is a scheme of characteristic p. f: X -> S is proper and smooth of relative dimension n. X' = X^{(p/S)} is the Frobenius twist, g: X' -> S, and F_{X/S}: X -> X' is the relative Frobenius, so that F_X = (projection X' -> X) o F_{X/S}. 'Th. 3' is the theorem of the preceding pages: the trace of finite flat relative Frobenius on top forms, Tr_{F_{X/S}}: F_{X/S*} Omega^n_{X/S} -> Omega^n_{X'/S}, coincides with the Cartier operator C~. The previous page states this in residue form, res(C~ omega / f~_1..f~_n) = res(omega / f_1^p..f_n^p).

This page applies Th. 3 to global Grothendieck–Serre duality.
1. Take E locally free on X (the image also allows a more general object). Let E~ be its pull-back to X'. Then F_{X/S}^* E~ = F_X^* E = E^{(p)}.
2. Adjunction for F_{X/S} gives the 'Frobenius' map (*): Rg_*(E~) -> Rf_*(E^{(p)}). Its source is identified, subject to the base-change caveat made explicit on the next page, with F_S^* Rf_*(E) = Rf_*(E)^{(p)}. Grothendieck remarks that (*) is essentially the base-change morphism of the commutative square (F_X, F_S).
3. Transposing (*) by relative duality (dualizing complex Omega^n[n]) gives Rf_*(E^{(p)v} ⊗ Omega^n_{X/S}[n]) -> Rg_*(E~^v ⊗ Omega^n_{X'/S}[n]). The left side is Rg_* F_{X/S*}(...), since F_{X/S} is finite.
4. By duality for the finite flat morphism F_{X/S}, this transpose is induced by the trace (**): F_{X/S*}(E^{(p)v} ⊗ Omega^n_{X/S}) = E~^v ⊗ F_{X/S*}Omega^n_{X/S} -> E~^v ⊗ Omega^n_{X'/S}. This is the projection formula followed by the usual trace tensored with E~^v[n]. By Th. 3 that trace is the Cartier operator.
5. Conclusion (finished on the next page): the transpose of R^n g_*(E~) = R^n f_*(E)^{(p)} -> R^n f_*(E^{(p)}) is f_*(E^{(p)v} ⊗ Omega^n) -> g_*(E~^v ⊗ Omega^n_{X'/S}), given by Cartier with coefficients.
6. For E = O_X: the p-linear Frobenius (Hasse–Witt) on R^n f_* O_X is Serre-dual to the Cartier operator on f_* Omega^n_{X/S}. More generally, Frobenius on R^i f_* O is dual to the map C~ induces on R^{n-i} f_* Omega^n. The next page goes on to R^1 f_* O = Lie Pic and to Verschiebung, i.e. Cartier–Manin / Hasse–Witt duality.

The problem served is a duality-theoretic proof that the Hasse–Witt matrix and the Cartier–Manin matrix are transposes, in families and with coefficients, as an application of 'trace of Frobenius = Cartier'.
errors: The identification Rg_*(E~) ≅ Rf_*(E)^{(p)} = F_S^* Rf_*(E) is flat base change along F_S. F_S is not flat unless S is regular-ish (e.g. smooth over a perfect field) or perfect. Otherwise it requires cohomology commuting with base change. The page states it as an equality; the next page adds 'sous réserve de commutation à F_S'.

Notation is loose. In the transposed map the source should be Rg_* of F_{X/S*}(...) (the marginal correction writes Rg_*(Rf_{X/S*}(...))), but the line itself writes Rf_* on both sides. Ě^{(p)} should be read as (E^{(p)})^v = (E^v)^{(p)}. Ω^n_{X/S}~ ≅ Ω^n_{X'/S} by base change of differentials.

The cancelled line [H^i(X,E) -> H^i(X',E~) -> H^i(X,E^{(p)})] treats the first arrow as a morphism. It is only p-linear (or a base change), which is presumably why it was struck out. No mathematical error remains in the final text.

ideas.what: Trace of relative Frobenius on top-degree differentials equals the Cartier operator (Th. 3, here applied).
ideas.modern_name: Tr_{F} = C on ω_X; trace map of Frobenius (Frobenius splitting theory)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore from Cartier/Grothendieck duality. Appears in Kunz, Lipman, Mehta–Ramanathan, Brion–Kumar (Frobenius splitting), Katz.

ideas.what: Transpose under Grothendieck–Serre duality of the Frobenius map on R^n f_*(E) is the Cartier operator with coefficients E^v on f_*(E^v ⊗ Ω^n).
ideas.modern_name: Duality between Frobenius action on coherent cohomology and Cartier operator (Cartier–Manin/Hasse–Witt duality, Frobenius-trace duality used in F-singularities/Cartier modules)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (1958, curves), Cartier, Manin (1963), Katz (Hasse–Witt computations, 1970s), Oda (1969); Blickle–Böckle (Cartier modules, 2011) for the sheaf version.

ideas.what: Frobenius map on cohomology viewed as the base-change morphism for the square (F_X, F_S).
ideas.modern_name: Linearized Frobenius via relative Frobenius/base change

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a clean, careful derivation of a classical fact (Hasse–Witt/Frobenius dual to Cartier via trace = Cartier). It is done in families and with vector-bundle coefficients, which is natural but well known in later literature (Katz, Oda, Cartier-module theory). There are no new constructions or unexplored threads beyond the base-change caveat.
transcription_corrections: The parenthesis after 'module loc. libre sur X' is hard to read. '(ou cristal ...)' is uncertain; it could be '(ou complexe parfait ...)' or similar.
The marginal label near the struck line reads like 'dit "Frobenius"', and the word above it ('polin'/'primaire') is illegible. It is not clearly 'primaire'.
In the transposed map, the target sheaf is written Ω^n_{X/S} with a tilde (i.e. Ω~^n ≅ Ω^n_{X'/S}). The source should be read as Rg_* ∘ F_{X/S*}, as indicated in the marginal addition.
Page number 179 appears at the bottom left. There is a faint marginal note at the lower left ('Agenda ...'?) which is not transcribed and is not mathematical.
